T: There are two kinds of people. Those who eat, and those who cook.
D: Three gunslingers race each other to a fortune in gold buried in a Civil War cemetery.
P: Serve the mains when Angel Eyes sits down to eat at the farmer's table.
S: Tuco marching Blondie across the desert
Corn tortillas cut into wedges, fried at 180C until crisp, tossed in salt and chilli, with a smoky charred tomato salsa.
Father Ramirez's focaccia and warm olives
the mission where Tuco's brother is a priest

Dimpled rosemary focaccia baked golden in good oil, with olives warmed through with orange peel, fennel seed and chilli. Mix 500g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 2 tsp salt and 400ml warm water and prove for 2 hours. Tip into an oiled 30 x 20cm tin with 4 tbsp olive oil, stretch to the edges, dimple with your fingers and prove 30 minutes. Scatter rosemary and flaky salt and bake at 220C for 22 minutes. Warm 300g mixed olives in olive oil with orange peel, 1 tsp fennel seeds and chilli flakes for 5 minutes.
the gold buried in the grave
Small potatoes sliced into coins, roasted at 220C in olive oil until golden and crisp, salted, with a garlic aioli.
M: the meal Angel Eyes eats at the farmer's table
Borlotti beans simmered 2 hours with smoked ham hock, onion, garlic, tomato and rosemary until thick, with crusty bread.
Tuco's spaghetti with beef and pork ragù
Tuco and his brother at the mission

Spaghetti tossed through a slow-cooked beef and pork ragù with red wine and tomato, finished with pecorino, chilli oil and torn basil. Brown 500g beef mince and 300g pork mince. Add 1 diced onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick and 3 garlic cloves and cook 8 minutes. Pour in 150ml red wine, then 2 tins crushed tomatoes and 2 tbsp tomato paste, and simmer gently for 2 hours, adding water if needed. Cook 500g spaghetti, toss through the ragù with a splash of pasta water, then top with grated pecorino, chilli oil and basil.
W: the graveyard where the gold is buried
Chocolate mousse in cups, topped with crushed chocolate biscuit soil and a little gold-wrapped chocolate coin buried in each.
K: Rye whisky stirred down with demerara syrup, orange bitters and a strip of orange peel, served over one big ice cube in a heavy glass. Stir 60g demerara sugar with 60ml hot water until dissolved, then cool. For each drink, stir 60ml rye whisky, 10ml of the syrup and 2 dashes of orange bitters with ice for 30 seconds. Strain over a large ice cube in a heavy glass. Twist a strip of orange peel over the top and drop it in.

s.note: Tuco marching Blondie across the desert
s.how: Cut 12 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C until crisp, then toss in salt and chilli powder. Char 4 tomatoes and half an onion in a dry pan until blackened. Chop together with lime juice and salt for a smoky salsa and serve with the chips.

s.note: the gold buried in the grave
s.how: Slice 800g small potatoes into thick coins and toss in olive oil and salt. Spread on a tray and roast at 220C for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Stir a crushed garlic clove into mayonnaise for aioli and serve the coins in a pile beside it.

m.note: the meal Angel Eyes eats at the farmer's table
m.how: Soak 400g dried borlotti beans overnight and drain. Soften a diced onion and garlic, then add the beans, a smoked ham hock, a can of crushed tomatoes, rosemary and water to cover. Simmer for 2 hours until thick, shred the ham back in and serve with Italian bread.

w.note: the graveyard where the gold is buried
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks and whip 300ml cream. Fold the yolks into the chocolate, then fold in the cream and whites. Spoon into cups with a chocolate coin buried in each, chill and top with crushed chocolate biscuits.

d.how: Stir 60g demerara sugar with 60ml hot water until dissolved, then cool. For each drink, stir 60ml rye whisky, 10ml of the syrup and 2 dashes of orange bitters with ice for 30 seconds. Strain over a large ice cube in a heavy glass. Twist a strip of orange peel over the top and drop it in.
